deep.reconstruction:
Context: Math.34 is Gauss's axiomatic development of the theory of parallels without the parallel postulate (cf. the 1831 notes and the letter to Schumacher of 1831). A ray BN.. is parallel to a ray AM.. when the two do not meet, and every ray from A drawn inside the angle BAM meets BN... Previous page: transitivity of parallelism (Th. 5) and a line lying between two parallels being parallel to both (Th. 6). This page continues with Th. 7 and a struck-out Th. 8.

Th. 7 (two parallel rays, prolonged backwards, cannot meet on that side).
Assume the lines AM and BN meet at P on their backward prolongations, beyond A and beyond B. Choose Q on line BN, past P on the backward side. Draw line QA and continue it past A.

Implicit step, mine: this continuation lies inside the angle BAM, for two reasons.
- Line BN crosses line AM at P, and B and Q lie on opposite sides of P. So B and Q are on opposite sides of line AM. The ray from A away from Q is therefore on B's side of AM.
- P and Q both lie on the ray from B opposite to N. So they are on the same side of line AB. P lies on the ray from A opposite to M, so P, and hence Q, are on the side of AB opposite to M. The ray from A away from Q is therefore on M's side of AB.

By the definition of parallel, this ray meets BN at some point R. Q and R are distinct, since R is on the forward side and Q on the backward side. So line QA and line BN are two distinct lines through Q and R. This is absurd: two points determine one line. QED.

Th. 8 (struck out). Claim: for parallels AM.., BN.. and transversal AB, angle BAM + angle ABN <= 2R. Gauss notes that this is already demonstrable from Euclid I.27 (the standard proof of I.27 via I.16).
The struck-out proof runs as follows.
1. Suppose BAM + ABN > 2R.
2. Prolong BN backward to K. The adjacent angle KBA = 2R - ABN is then less than BAM.
3. Lay off angle BAL equal to angle KBA. The manuscript writes AKB, evidently meant ABK. Then AL lies strictly inside the angle BAM.
4. By the definition of parallel, AL meets BN at a point P.
5. Take Q on BK with BQ = AP.
6. Triangles ABQ and BAP are congruent by SAS: AB is common, BQ = AP, and angle ABQ = angle KBA = angle BAP. Hence angle BAQ = angle ABP.
7. The page ends here. Implied completion, mine: angle QAB + angle BAP = ABN + KBA = 2R. So Q, A, P are collinear, and the line QP meets line BN in the two distinct points Q and P. Contradiction.
This is exactly the Euclid I.16/I.27 congruence argument, which is presumably why Gauss crossed it out as superfluous.
errors: In the struck-out proof, 'BAL = AKB' should read BAL = ABK (= KBA). AKB is not a meaningful angle here, since K is on line BN. This is a slip.
'AL liegt zwischen AK und AB' (or AB und AK): logically AL must lie between AM and AB, i.e. inside angle BAM, for the definition of parallel to apply. This is probably a slip or a misreading.
In Th. 7, Gauss does not justify that QA prolonged beyond A falls inside angle BAM. The justification is supplied in the reconstruction. It is easy but uses plane-separation (Pasch-type) properties.
The struck-out proof breaks off before the final contradiction (collinearity of Q, A, P). It was abandoned rather than wrong.

results.what: Parallel rays (Gauss's 'asymptotic' definition) cannot meet when prolonged backwards
results.modern_name: Parallel (limiting) lines do not intersect: a basic lemma of absolute/hyperbolic geometry
results.usually_credited_to: Lemma implicit in Lobachevsky (1829/1840) and J. Bolyai (1832); Gauss's own 1831 notes on parallels were published in Werke VIII (1900)

results.what: Interior angles on one side of a transversal of two parallels sum to at most two right angles (struck out, with the I.27-style congruence proof)
results.modern_name: Consequence of Euclid I.16/I.27 (exterior angle theorem); angle sum <= 180 degrees in absolute geometry (Saccheri-Legendre type)

deep.surprise_reason: This is part of Gauss's known axiomatic treatment of parallels (1831 era), published in Werke VIII. The lemmas are elementary absolute-geometry facts, and Gauss's work on non-Euclidean foundations is well documented.

checkable.sympy: import sympy as sp; ABN=sp.Symbol('ABN'); KBA=sp.pi-ABN; sp.simplify(KBA+ABN-sp.pi)==0
checkable.asserts: The adjacent (supplementary) angle KBA equals 2R - ABN.

checkable.sympy: import sympy as sp; BAM,ABN=sp.symbols('BAM ABN',positive=True); sp.simplify((sp.pi-ABN<BAM).subs({BAM:2,ABN:2}))
checkable.asserts: If BAM + ABN > pi then KBA = pi - ABN < BAM (numeric instance 2 + 2 > pi).

checkable.sympy: import sympy as sp; ABN,KBA=sp.symbols('ABN KBA'); BAQ=ABN; BAP=KBA; sp.simplify((BAQ+BAP).subs(KBA,sp.pi-ABN))
checkable.asserts: After the congruence, angle QAB + angle BAP = ABN + KBA = pi, so Q, A, P are collinear (completion of the struck-out proof).

transcription_corrections: Struck-out proof: 'BAL = AKB' is as written but should mean BAL = ABK (KBA); note as an author slip.
Struck-out proof: the phrase read as 'zwischen AK und AB' may be 'zwischen AB und AK'. Either way the sense requires 'zwischen AM und AB'.
In the struck-out proof, 'man mache also' appears with an interlinear insertion (apparently 'machen'/'mache') above the line. Minor.
'adhib. der Par.' = adhibita definitione der Parallelen, i.e. using the definition of parallels.
